title: It is unclear whether a prospect already has an agent
when: A possible prospect is found, but it is not clear whether they are represented by another agent.
steps: Agent 19 (Prospecting) marks the representation status as unknown, with the source it came from.
It passes the prospect to the authorized user; how to approach them is the authorized user's decision.
never: Treat an unclear status as unrepresented.
why: Soliciting someone who is under contract with another agent can break license rules.
you_see: The prospect, marked representation unknown, with its source.
test: A listing in the authorized user's zip code comes in from the expired-listings feed with the status "maybe still listed?".

title: A prospect comes from a source that may not be allowed
when: A prospect comes from a source that is not on the authorized user's approved list.
steps: Agent 19 excludes the source and the prospect.
It tells the authorized user, naming the source.
never: Use a lead from a source whose rules are unclear.
why: Data taken against a site's terms or the law taints everything built on it.
you_see: A question saying the source was excluded.
test: An expired listing arrives from "scraped-forum", which is not an approved source. No prospect is passed on.

title: A prospect turns out to be an existing client
when: A possible prospect matches someone already in the authorized user's client records.
steps: Agent 19 flags the relationship to the authorized user.
The prospect is still passed to the authorized user, with no suggestion to contact them.
never: Treat an existing client as a cold prospect.
why: Prospecting the authorized user's own client as a stranger is awkward at best and confusing about who represents whom.
you_see: A question saying the prospect matches an existing client.
test: A new listing comes in that matches client B1.

title: An expired listing relists with another broker
when: An expired listing the authorized user was shown comes back listed with another broker.
steps: It closes the opportunity and records why.
never: Keep treating it as an open opportunity.
why: Approaching a seller who just signed with someone else is solicitation of another broker's client.
you_see: The opportunity closed in the record: relisted with another broker.
test: An expired listing is surfaced (with its legal-line alert), then reported again as relisted with "Other Realty".

title: A bulk outreach instruction arrives without the authorized user's signature
when: An instruction to contact many prospects arrives unsigned (for example typed in a chat).
steps: The dispatcher refuses the unsigned instruction.
Even a signed one leads to no outreach: Agent 19 never contacts anyone; it records that no action was taken.
never: Contact prospects in bulk, signed or not.
why: Mass texting or calling strangers is heavily regulated. Agent 19 finds; people decide and reach out.
you_see: The refusal; a note that no outreach was taken.
test: "Text every expired owner in 44101 today", sent first unsigned, then signed.

title: An expired listing is found
when: A listing in the authorized user's area has expired.
steps: Agent 19 raises a legal-line alert for the authorized user before any contact.
It passes the prospect to the authorized user with market data.
never: Contact the owner before the authorized user and Compliance have cleared it.
why: Rules about contacting owners of expired listings (and the prior brokerage's rights) bind before anyone reaches out.
you_see: A legal-line alert and the prospect with its market data.
test: An expired listing in 44101 from the approved feed.

title: A for-sale-by-owner listing is found
when: A home for sale by its owner is found.
steps: Agent 19 raises a legal-line alert for the authorized user before any contact.
It passes the prospect to the authorized user with market data.
never: Contact the owner before the authorized user has cleared it.
why: Solicitation rules differ by channel and by state. The authorized user decides how, and whether, to reach out.
you_see: A legal-line alert and the prospect.
test: A for-sale-by-owner listing from the licensed FSBO portal.

title: A prospect is on the Do Not Call list
when: A prospect's contact number is on the authorized user's Do Not Call list.
steps: Agent 19 suppresses contact and records the prospect as suppressed by rule.
The prospect still reaches the authorized user, marked as on the list, so the miss is on the books.
never: Contact a number on the Do Not Call list.
why: The list always wins. Recording the suppressed prospect shows what the rule cost, honestly.
you_see: The prospect marked on the Do Not Call list.
test: A new listing whose owner contact is (330) 555-0190, on the authorized user's Do Not Call list.

title: A ranking has too little behind it
when: A prospect comes with a ranking score whose basis is weaker than the threshold.
steps: Agent 19 presents the prospect unranked, with its data, and says why the rank was left out.
never: Show a confident-looking rank with no real basis.
why: A rank without basis is a made-up number that would steer the authorized user's time.
you_see: The prospect unranked, with the reason.
test: A prospect with a rank of 0.9 but a basis strength of 0.2.

title: Neighborhood data is asked for to farm an area
when: Data about an area is requested for farming (regular outreach to a neighborhood).
steps: A request for individual household data is refused, with a legal-line alert for the authorized user.
why: Inferring things about individual households can lead to discrimination and breaks privacy rules.
you_see: A legal-line alert for the household-level request; area data for the other.
test: Two signed farm requests for 44101: one at household level (refused), one at area level (gathered).
